bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cessation of all business operations — the only manufacturing plant has been permanently shut — Manufacturing at the Company's only plant in Bengaluru was discontinued with effect from 15 December 2025 and the plant was subsequently shut down. The MD&A states that the Company has no plans to restart operations in the foreseeable future, leaving the Company without an operating business.
- Financial statements not prepared on a going concern basis — The Board's Report states that, as the Board of Directors are in the process of deciding the future course of the Company's activity, the financial statements have not been prepared on a going concern basis. The Company's future as an operating entity is therefore undecided.
- Irreversibility of the closure — Factory Licence and sanctioned power surrendered — Following the cessation of manufacturing activities, the Factory Licence and sanctioned power facilities were surrendered, so any resumption of manufacturing would require fresh regulatory approvals and power sanction rather than a simple restart.
- Pending labour disputes arising from retrenchment — Substantially the entire workforce was retrenched following the shutdown. The Board's Report records that labour disputes are pending before various courts and other judicial forums and that management intends to maintain the status quo, leaving an unresolved legal overhang.
- Loss of the contract-manufacturing relationship underpinning volumes — The Company manufactured grinding media for its holding company AIA Engineering Ltd. under a Contract Manufacturing Agreement running 5 years from 1 January 2024, entered into to fully utilise the installed capacity. With manufacturing ceased, the arrangement that absorbed the Company's capacity no longer supports operations.
- Single-segment, single-product, single-site concentration — The Company primarily operated in only one segment, the manufacture of High Chrome Grinding Media Balls, from a single plant in Bengaluru, so it had no other business or site to fall back on when that plant closed.
- Collapse in production and sales volumes during the year — The Board's Report attributes lower production and sales to the closure of plant operations from 15 December 2025, and the MD&A explains the deterioration in interest coverage, operating profit margin, net profit margin and return on net worth by the cessation of operations in the second half of the financial year together with increased fixed overheads and employee retrenchment related payments.
- End-market exposure and external factors flagged in the cautionary statement — The MD&A cautionary statement flags economic conditions affecting demand, supply and price conditions in the domestic and overseas markets in which the Company operates, changes in government regulations, and tax laws and other statutes, as factors that could cause actual results to differ from forward-looking statements.

business.body: Welcast Steels manufactured high chrome grinding media balls in sizes ranging from 40 mm to 125 mm in diameter, with alloy compositions containing 12% to 28% chromium, produced using the casting process. The products offer wear and corrosion resistance and mechanical strength at elevated operating temperatures, and were used for grinding applications in the Cement, Mining and Thermal Power industries. The Company operated in only one segment, and manufactured grinding media of different grades for AIA Engineering Ltd. under a contract manufacturing agreement using technical know-how provided by AIA, while remaining free to manufacture for other parties.

outlook.body:
- Permanent closure of the only manufacturing plant at Bengaluru with effect from 15 December 2025, following a Board resolution of 15 October 2025, including surrender of the Factory Licence and sanctioned power facilities.
- No restart of operations in the foreseeable future and no plans for any expansion; all business activities have been closed down.
- Retrenchment of substantially the entire workforce in accordance with applicable labour laws, retaining only eight employees for post-closure activities and statutory compliance.
- The Board of Directors is in the process of deciding the future course of the Company's activity; financial statements have accordingly not been prepared on a going concern basis.
- Maintain the status quo while labour disputes remain pending before various courts and other judicial forums.
- Continued judicious management of working capital, receivables and inventories, with other working capital parameters kept under strict check through continuous monitoring.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: There is no expansion programme. The Board of Directors resolved at its meeting held on 15 October 2025 to close down the Company's only plant in Bengaluru, and the plant formally shut down from 15 December 2025. Following the cessation of manufacturing activities the Factory Licence and sanctioned power facilities were surrendered, substantially the entire workforce was retrenched and only eight employees were retained for post-closure activities and statutory compliance. The MD&A states there is no capex plan as the Company has closed down all its business activities, and the Board's Report states that there are no plans for any expansion as the operation of the plant is permanently closed and that no further capital expenditure is to be incurred. The Company has no plans to resume operations in the foreseeable future, and the Board is in the process of deciding the future course of the Company's activity.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- High chrome grinding media balls serve grinding applications in the Cement, Mining and Thermal Power industries, where ores and other materials are reduced to fine particle sizes to facilitate liberation and subsequent processing of valuable minerals.
- Production and sales fell year on year because of the closure of plant operations from 15 December 2025.
- Management states that, with business operations permanently closed down, there are no major risks and concerns relating to business activities.
- The Contract Manufacturing Agreement with AIA Engineering Ltd. was entered into to fully utilise the installed capacity of the Company.
